title: userfaultfd_move accepts a recycled swap entry while retaining the wrong folio

classification.cwe_mapping_note: These are evaluator classifications; the linked Linux CVE announcement does not assign an official CWE.

finding.stale_identity: The move path retains a folio obtained from a lockless swap-cache lookup and later revalidates only the numeric source PTE swap entry. The entry can be freed and rebound while the retained folio no longer represents it.
finding.control_flow: The source PTE is observed as entry 7; source folio 100 is swapped in and frees 7; replacement folio 200 is swapped out under 7 and becomes the lookup candidate; 200 is swapped in and frees 7; source folio 100 is swapped out under 7; the final integer PTE comparison succeeds and candidate 200 is moved.
finding.impact: The wrong folio is moved and accounted to the faulting VMA, modeling the bad RSS-counter state and BUG_ON described by the Linux CVE announcement. The announcement does not establish user-data corruption.
finding.security_property: A recycled swap-entry value must not authenticate folio identity. The folio moved from a swap PTE must be the folio currently bound to that entry after the candidate is locked.
finding.expected_fix: After acquiring the candidate folio lock, look up the swap cache again and require the entry-to-folio identity to match before moving it; also recheck swap-cache presence under the source PTE lock when the initial lookup found no folio.
finding.model_boundary: The request uses one bounded 4 KiB MiniMM note and three nonzero uint32 identifiers. It performs deterministic metadata transitions only and never creates host userfaultfd state, enables swap, changes host page tables, runs a thread race, accesses freed memory, or triggers a kernel assertion.
